POWER7 and later IBM server processors have a register called the
Program Priority Register (PPR)
each hardware CPU SMT thread
column2: and affects how fast it runs compared

column1: to other SMT threads.  This priority can be controlled by writing to
the PPR or by use of a set of instructions of the form or rN
which are otherwise no-ops but have been defined to set the priority
to particular levels.
This adds code to context switch the PPR when entering and exiting
guests and to make the PPR value accessible through the SET/GET_ONE_REG
interface.  When entering the guest
column2: we set the PPR as late as

column1: possible
column2: because if we are setting a low thread priority it will

column1: make the code run slowly from that point on.  Similarly
first-level interrupt handlers save the PPR value in the PACA very
early on
column2: and set the thread priority to the medium level

column1: the interrupt handling code runs at a reasonable speed.
